title: Sara Duterte to Claire Castro: Are you admitting Marcos ordered 'kidnapping' of FPRRD?
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday questioned the supposed contrasting statements of Palace Press Officer Usec. Claire Castro with those of President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos regarding the…

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday questioned the supposed contrasting statements of Palace Press Officer Usec. Claire Castro with those of President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos regarding the arrest and transfer of former President Rodrigo Duterte to The Hague.

Duterte said this in a press conference, reacting to the earlier statement of Castro that surrendering Rodrigo Duterte to the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC) was allowed under Republic Act 9851.
The Palace official also said the matter had nothing to do with sovereignty as the Philippines was a voluntary member of the ICC before it withdrew from the Rome Statute in 2019.

The Vice President, in response, pointed out that Castro’s statement was seemingly contrary to the previous remark of Marcos that his administration would not cooperate with the inquiry of the ICC into the case of his predecessor.

“Nagtataka ako bakit ganyan ang sagot niya. Quite the opposite sa sagot ni President Marcos noong tinatanong natin siya noon ‘di ba about ICC cooperation. And then he answered that ‘we shall not cooperate in any way, shape, or form with the ICC,’” Sara Duterte said.

(I wonder why she gave such an answer. It’s quite the opposite of the statement of President Marcos when we asked him about ICC cooperation. He said that ‘we shall not cooperate in any way, shape, or form with the ICC.’)
She also cited an official correspondence from the Office of the President, where Marcos supposedly said that the ICC is an affront to Philippine sovereignty.
“I think may split personality na ata ang mga tao diyan sa Office of the…President,” she said.
(I think the people at the Office of the…President might have developed a split personality.)
“This is an example of our government right now. Sinasalamin nila ‘yung P20 ang kilo ng bigas (they’re reflecting the P20-per-kilo rice promise),” she added.
Duterte further asked if it was Marcos who was lying in the official correspondence or if it was Castro with her recent statement.

“At inaamin na ba ngayon, kasi nagde-deny sila noon ‘di ba na the government had anything to do with the kidnapping, it was an Interpol red notice. So ngayon ba, inaamin na niya, ni Claire Castro, na si President Marcos talaga ang nag-utos sa pag-kidnap kay President Duterte?”

(And are they admitting it now, since they previously denied that the government had anything to do with the kidnapping, claiming it was an Interpol red notice? Is Claire Castro admitting now that it was actually President Marcos who ordered the kidnapping of President Duterte?)
The Vice President also took a jab at people who take illegal drugs.
“Epekto kasi minsan ‘yan talaga ng droga, sa totoo lang. Hindi ako nagbibiro. I am not joking. ‘Yung mga nagdo-droga, minsan talaga sabog na ’yung pag-iisip nila,” she said.
(To be honest, that is sometimes an effect of drugs. I’m not joking. Sometimes the minds of people who use drugs are completely scrambled.) —LDF, GMA News
